revision: R3 (2026-11-06): serving relay at the pass; replaces the R2.2 four-bowl microwave relay
embodiment: Dual ARX X5, stationary island mount (common rig: bases side by side at x=0.00 / 0.60 m, y=-0.255 m, 0.60 m apart, facing +y; RoboDojo head camera 0.04 m forward of the base midpoint, 0.543 m above the mount tops, 60 deg down, Gemini 345Lg 640x480; D435 wrist cameras on link6); ready pose q=[0, .94, 1.34, -1.40, 0, 0]
time_origin: t=0 at the first agent observation; the pickups keep their times while the agent deliberates
interface: 16-value joint targets (x5/interface.py); observations: head and wrist RGB, joints, tool poses, gripper widths, instruction
status: design + static initial state + task/process/scoring model + Isaac Sim physics episode with a privileged oracle controller (sim.py), validated against the task model and an independent trajectory check, and recorded (one reference episode, seed 0, medium)
title: Serve the ordered meals at the pass
category: C qualified throughput (single-plate pass, two-arm relay)
household_need: Lunch orders go out one plate at a time: a waiter collects at set times, each time a particular meal.
instruction: Serve the meals on the serving board in the order given. The board holds one bowl; a waiter takes it at each pickup time. Bring the waiting bowls to the mat, then on to the board. A meal is served once its bowl stands upright and released on the board; the waiter takes whatever bowl is there, and a late meal after it has stood there 1 second. A bowl tilted more than 40 degrees, even in a gripper, or off the counter counts as dropped and fails the task.
why_r3: R2.2 ran 600 process seconds (800 / 600 / 400 s at easy / medium / hard), a quarter of the simulated time of the household suite, most of it waiting on the microwave; one microwave turnaround alone took the oracle about 40 s. R3 keeps the bowls, the staging mat, the board and the handle grasps, and runs 60 process seconds.
core_interventions: left arm: take the next wanted meal from the counter by handle B and set it down on the staging mat
right arm: take the staged meal from the mat by handle A and set it down on the serving board
keep the board free for one bowl: set the next meal down only after the waiter has taken the previous one

process.state: which bowl rests on the board; which bowls the waiter has taken
process.model: at each pickup time the waiter takes the bowl resting released and upright on the board; it qualifies if it is the meal wanted at that pickup

per_seed.order: permutation of the four meals (curry, rice, soup, pasta); the first wanted meal starts on the mat
per_seed.slots: which waiting meal stands in which of the three counter slots
per_seed.jitter: counter slots +-1.2 cm in x and y, +-8 deg in yaw

process.cue: the instruction names the order and the pickup times (the card on the counter only states the rule); the meals are told apart by their food

timing.event: a pickup qualifies when the wanted meal rests released and upright on the board at its pickup time
timing.rule: C-class stream task (score_version 2, docs/c-class-timing.md): each order is a job, its deadline the pickup time, its time when its meal was set down on the board (it must stay there until the waiter takes it). A pickup without its meal leaves the order open: the waiter takes that meal once it has rested on the board for 1 s. The pickups are 4 / 2 / 1 x the hard schedule at easy / medium / hard (see difficulty). Horizon 1.25 x the last pickup; the episode ends 2 s after the last pickup once every ordered meal is served. Reported: qualified meals, slack (pickup minus time on the board) per order

physical: no bowl dropped or tipped over (tilt > 40 deg)
every ordered meal served by the end of the episode, late or not (on the board or taken by the waiter)
completion.temporal: every ordered meal on the board by its pickup (judge_stream; no physical terms)

failures: wrong meal on the board at a pickup (violation; the order does not qualify)
permitted: serving a meal long before its pickup, if the board is free
arm_roles: left: counter slots to the staging mat (handle B); right: staging mat to the serving board (handle A). One arm at a time works at the mat.

staging_mat.note: on the line between the bases: the only place where one handle axis suits both arms (R2.2 position); wrist-camera view only (x5/visibility.py)

serving_board.note: in front of the right arm, out of the left arm's reach

why: An X5 holds a bowl by a handle only beyond about 0.28 m from its own base, so neither arm reaches both the counter slots (front left) and the board (front right).

The slots face the left arm (handle B toward its base) and lie outside the right arm's reach; the left arm carries along arcs that keep its hand more than 0.3 m from its base and waits 0.3 m from the right arm's route while the mat is busy.

R2.2 put the waiting bowls in front of the right base, where the left arm unfolded over the board and could stage only after each pickup; R3's slots keep the arms on their own sides, so staging overlaps serving.

demo_guidance: Bowls have two 20 deg upswept lug handles; every grasp pinches a handle with the tool pitched 20 deg down (pads parallel to the handle) and closes each jaw until contact.
Carrying a bowl: ramp speed and turn rate (0.25 m/s^2, 1 rad/s^2); a jerk rotates the bowl about the pinch axis.
The right arm holds the next meal beside the board (16 cm from the board bowl) until the pickup, then sets it down.
open_items: the waiter is appliance logic: the bowl on the board is moved off the counter at the pickup time
bowl mass 0.14 kg with food; 20 N/jaw clamp is an assumption

assets.name: ServingBoard
assets.role: the pass: one bowl, collected by the waiter

difficulty.rule: C-class stream rule (2026-11-09, docs/c-class-timing.md): the same four orders at every tier; the pickups are m x the hard schedule (m = 4 / 2 / 1 at easy / medium / hard), which stretches the first pickup and the intervals alike; time_scale is 1 and nothing else changes; max_time = H = 1.25 x the last pickup. Hard is a first pickup at 10.53 s and one every 12.96 s, the tightest such schedule (0.01 s steps) the slowest oracle meets, from 28 oracle runs on seeds 0-6 and 50-56: 14 with the board freed 1 s after each set-down, so that no pickup held the oracle back, and 14 at this schedule. Until 2026-11-09: time_scale 0.75 / 1.0 / 1.5 divided the process-second pickups 20 / 32 / 44 / 56 s, and hard took three orders at 14 / 26 / 39 s.

hard.note: slowest oracle set-down per order 10.524 / 23.484 / 36.344 / 49.204 s (every seed; seed 2): the second order binds (10.53 + 12.96 >= 23.484), the third and fourth keep 0.11 and 0.21 s against the up to 0.1 s by which moving a pickup shifts later set-downs. All 14 seeds at hard: every order on the board by its pickup (smallest slack 0.006 s), physical, all_done. The next meal arrives beside the board about 8.8 s or more after each pickup, so the board never holds the oracle back at hard
